purpose: Teach: 実戦/石綿/快晴/歳児/ミドル/水上/境内/パース

lines.speaker: hiroshi_boss
lines.jp: 当社、実戦演習を社員研修に取り入れろ
lines.en: I want us to introduce practical drills into our employee training program.
lines.style: Direct, measured authority. Clean attack on the first syllable. No negotiation in the tone—this is a directive, not a discussion. Slight pause after the core statement.

lines.speaker: kenji_office
lines.jp: はい。石綿フリーの建材を採用します
lines.en: Understood. We'll switch to asbestos-free building materials.
lines.style: Respectful acknowledgment with professional focus. Steady, unhurried delivery. Each phrase lands clearly but without heaviness. Kenji accepting and translating the order into concrete action.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_boss
lines.jp: 当社、快晴予報日には屋外イベントを企画しろ
lines.en: And I want us to plan outdoor events on days with clear weather forecasts.
lines.style: Another directive, same composed authority as the first. Slightly warmer—there's something pragmatic and almost shrewd here. Enumerating without laboring.

lines.speaker: kenji_office
lines.jp: はい。三歳児向けの教育玩具事業も検討します
lines.en: Understood. We're also looking into developing educational toys for young children.
lines.style: Kenji in step, translating again. A beat of genuine thinking in his voice—he's not parroting, he's connecting the directive to a parallel initiative. Warm professionalism.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_boss
lines.jp: 当社、ミドル層向け商品ラインを強化しろ
lines.en: We need to strengthen our product line for the middle market.
lines.style: Third directive. Same composed tempo. The authority here is so settled it doesn't need to be loud. Hiroshi is clear, expecting execution, not surprise.

lines.speaker: kenji_office
lines.jp: はい。水上スポーツ用品の販売拡大します
lines.en: Understood. We'll expand our water sports equipment sales.
lines.style: Kenji continuing the pattern. Still present, still professional. There's a rhythm building—he's kept pace and will keep pace. Steady, capable tone.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_boss
lines.jp: 当社、境内市場、つまり地域祭事の出店も検討しろ
lines.en: Consider developing a presence at local festival markets—the boundary between our usual and these community spaces.
lines.style: Fourth directive, but with a subtle shift: Hiroshi is slightly more reflective here. He explains his thinking a little—'boundary markets'—as if testing whether Kenji follows. Still authoritative, but inviting alignment more than blind execution.

lines.speaker: kenji_office
lines.jp: はい。製品図面のパースを精密化します
lines.en: Understood. I'll also refine the precision of our product renderings and technical drawings.
lines.style: Final acknowledgment. Kenji has caught the expanded vision. His tone solidifies—there's a sense of closure, of full agreement, of having heard all the pieces. Slightly more deliberate than before.
